sections.h2: What are the choices for selling a house in Stevens Point?
sections.html:
You can list with an agent, sell on your own, or accept a cash offer for the house as-is. Stevens Point has a large rental and student market, so the condition of the house and who lives in it often decides the route.

A traditional listing suits a house that shows well and can wait for a buyer's inspection and financing. A direct cash sale fits a house with deferred repairs, a tenant in place, or an estate that wants a date certain. Price the cash route against what you would net after repairs, carrying costs and the time a listing takes.

  • Owner-occupied house in good order: a listing usually reaches the most buyers.
  • Rental or student house with turnover problems: a buyer who already runs rentals may value it more than a first-time buyer does.
  • Inherited or vacant house: a cash sale avoids months of utilities, taxes and upkeep.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers say about the Stevens Point housing market?
sections.html:
Stevens Point is a renter-heavy city. Only 51.1 percent of housing units are owner-occupied, and the median owner-occupied home is valued at $195,400. The population estimate for 2025 is 26,377, up 2.8 percent from the 2020 base.

A bachelor's degree or higher is held by 37.9 percent of adults 25 and older. Treat the median value as a citywide yardstick, not an appraisal of your house.

sections.h2: What is Stevens Point like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Stevens Point is the seat of Portage County, set on the Wisconsin River in central Wisconsin. The Plover River joins the Wisconsin to the south and supplies much of the urban area's water. Plover, Whiting and Park Ridge sit next to the city, and the city's elevation is about 1,089 feet.

The first plat was laid out in 1847 and the city takes its name from George Stevens, who ran a supply business on the river during the logging era. The Stevens Point Area Public School District serves the city, with Stevens Point Area Senior High as its main high school, and Pacelli Catholic Schools operate alongside it. The University of Wisconsin-Stevens Point and Mid-State Technical College are both in the city.

Five routes cross the area: Interstate 39, U.S. 10, U.S. 51, Highway 54 and Highway 66. Stevens Point Transit runs local buses, and Central Wisconsin Airport is in Mosinee.

sections.h2: How do winters in Stevens Point affect a house?
sections.html:
Winters are long and cold. The 1991 to 2020 normals show a January average low of 7.1 degrees, a February record low of minus 48, and about 48.7 inches of snow in a year, with 33.97 inches of total precipitation.

Buyers and their inspectors focus on the roof, attic insulation, the furnace and the foundation after a winter like that. Keep furnace service records and any roof invoices together. The city requires sidewalk snow to be removed within 24 hours of the end of a snowfall, or 48 hours on streets without a boulevard, so a vacant house needs someone assigned to shovel while it is on the market.

sections.h2: Which Stevens Point city rules should I check before listing?
sections.html:
The city's housing ordinance brochure covers the points that most often catch sellers. Read it alongside the permit record for your address.

  • Permits are required for most remodeling, including structural work, siding, reroofing, a new water heater, furnace or air conditioner, sheds, fencing, demolition and electrical or plumbing beyond fixtures. Asking before you start avoids a double permit fee.
  • Lawns and weeds must stay under 9 inches, boulevard included. Unpaid city mowing is assessed to the property.
  • Occupancy is limited to two unrelated adults or one family unless the property holds a specific occupancy license. A buyer planning a student rental will ask about this.
  • Garbage and recycling carts go to the curb the evening before pickup and are stored at or behind the front plane of the dwelling.

If you took a loan from the city's Rental Improvement Program, its terms require the loan to be repaid in full before the property is sold, and a property in a 1 percent flood plain must carry flood insurance at least equal to the first mortgage plus the loan. Ask the Community Development Department for a payoff figure early.

sections.h2: What do I disclose and pay when I sell in Portage County?
sections.html:
Wisconsin law asks the owner of a one-to-four unit property to give the buyer a completed condition report within 10 days after a contract is accepted. If the report is late, the buyer has 2 business days after that 10-day period to rescind and recover deposits. Personal representatives, trustees, conservators and court-appointed fiduciaries who never occupied the house are excused from the report. The rules are in Chapter 709.

The seller also owes the state transfer fee of 30 cents per $100 of value under section 77.22. At the Stevens Point median value of $195,400, that is $586.20. The register of deeds collects it at recording, and an electronic transfer return must be filed first. Transfers by will, descent or survivorship and transfers from a parent to a child for nominal consideration are on the exemption list in section 77.25, but a sale to an outside buyer is a regular conveyance.

Deeds are recorded at the Portage County Register of Deeds, 1516 Church Street, Stevens Point. The city's loan program materials list a $30 mortgage recording fee at that office. Ask the register for the current charge on a deed before you mail one.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Stevens Point rental house with tenants in it?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer can purchase a rental with tenants in it. Gather the leases, rent records and deposit details so the buyer can see the terms, and ask a Wisconsin attorney how the leases affect your closing date.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer fee when I sell in Stevens Point?
faqs.a: The state fee is 30 cents per $100 of value, owed by the seller. A $200,000 sale carries a $600 fee. The Portage County Register of Deeds collects it when the deed is recorded, along with the recording fee.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for work I did before selling?
faqs.a: Most roofing, siding, furnace, water heater, fence and electrical work in Stevens Point needs a city permit. Contact the city's Inspection and Community Development staff at City Hall, 1515 Strongs Avenue, and ask what is on file for your address.

faqs.q: What if I owe money on a city Rental Improvement Program loan?
faqs.a: The program's terms say the loan must be repaid in full before the property is sold. Ask the Community Development Department for a payoff amount and have your title company include it on the closing statement.

faqs.q: Is a condition report required if I inherited the house?
faqs.a: Not if you are a personal representative, trustee, conservator or court-appointed fiduciary who never occupied the property. If you lived there, the report applies. A Wisconsin probate attorney can confirm which category you fall in.
